59783396.s: King Abdulaziz Castle is one of the forts built during the reign of King Abdulaziz in the period of the founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. It stands in the old Al Balda district of Haql governorate in the Tabuk region.
59783396.b: King Abdulaziz Castle is one of the forts built during the reign of King Abdulaziz in the period of the founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. It stands in the old Al Balda district of Haql governorate in the Tabuk region.

59783395.s: King Abdulaziz Castle was built in 1352 AH (1933 CE) on a raised hill overlooking the market from the west, to serve as the seat of Saudi government in the area. It is considered one of the most important forts in the Tabuk region and lies in Duba governorate, in north-western Saudi Arabia. Built on a high plateau to serve as the seat of the region's emirate, it is made of limestone in the style of the area's forts and has been restored as a tourist facility. The castle covers 1,000 square metres.

59783395.a: King Abdulaziz Castle, Al Balad, Duba

59783378.s: Al Azlam Castle lies in Wadi Al Aznam, south of the city of Duba, and was one of the stations on the Egyptian Hajj route during the late Islamic period. It consists of a large courtyard, interior units, rectangular and semicircular rooms, and a reception hall (diwan). The castle is built of dressed limestone, and its courtyard opens onto all the interior units, which include the rooms. It covers 1,500 square metres, stands very close to the main road linking Duba and Al Wajh, and is now surrounded by a wall to protect it.

59783376.s: Old Duba is the historic town of Duba, on the Red Sea. It has traditional stone buildings that reflect the coastal architecture of the area. King Abdulaziz Castle and the old market stand nearby, making it a distinctive stop for learning about the city's history.
59783376.b: Old Duba is the historic town of Duba, on the Red Sea. It has traditional stone buildings that reflect the coastal architecture of the area. King Abdulaziz Castle and the old market stand nearby, making it a distinctive stop for learning about the city's history.

59783373.s: The Old Souq in Al Wajh governorate, known in the past as "Al Manakha", is one of the main landmarks of the historic Al Balad district. It once had a gate controlling entry and exit. The souq was a centre of trade: Bedouin brought livestock, ghee, honey and firewood, while merchants supplied rice, wheat, fabrics, coffee, cardamom and sugar. It was linked to Al Wajh port, from which sailing ships set out for Red Sea ports.
59783373.b:
The Old Souq in Al Wajh governorate, known in the past as "Al Manakha", is one of the main landmarks of the historic Al Balad district. It once had a gate controlling entry and exit. The souq was a centre of trade: Bedouin brought livestock, ghee, honey and firewood, while merchants supplied rice, wheat, fabrics, coffee, cardamom and sugar. It was linked to Al Wajh port, from which sailing ships set out for Red Sea ports.

The souq is overlooked by the Souq Castle (the town castle), which stands on a high hill and dates to 1276 AH (1859 CE). It was built to protect the town and to oversee the port and the souq.
59783373.a: Al Balad District, Al Wajh Governorate, Tabuk Region

59783368.t: Al Zurayb Castle in Al Wajh
59783368.s: Al Zurayb Castle is a historic fortress in the east of Al Wajh governorate in the Tabuk region. A large fort built in the reign of Sultan Ahmed I in 1026 AH (1617 CE) to protect pilgrims and store their deposits and provisions, it has a foundation inscription at its entrance.
59783368.b:
Al Zurayb Castle is a historic fortress in the east of Al Wajh governorate in the Tabuk region. A large fort built in the reign of Sultan Ahmed I in 1026 AH (1617 CE) to protect pilgrims and store their deposits and provisions, it has a foundation inscription at its entrance.

The castle has a rectangular plan with four towers, one at each corner, and its entrance is on the western side. Inside, rooms surround the courtyard, and there are a mosque, a prayer area and a well. Three ponds are attached to the outside of its northern side. The castle takes a square form, with four round towers at its corners for observation and defence. Its plan shows a high level of building skill and precision, with right-angled corners and straight facades. A prominent gateway projects slightly from the western facade. The entrance gate is rectangular and wide, topped by a segmental arch and flanked by stone benches, and it was used to protect the castle door. The inner face of the gateway is distinguished by coloured stones that set it apart from the stones used outside. The facades have no architectural openings except for the arrow slits spread along the upper part of the building.

59783322.s: Ship Mountain is a mountain with geological and historical remains, located west of the city of Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia. It is called Ship Mountain because its formation looks very much like a ship.
59783322.b:
Ship Mountain is a mountain with geological and historical remains, located west of the city of Tabuk in north-western Saudi Arabia. It is called Ship Mountain because its formation looks very much like a ship.

The mountain bears many inscriptions and remains that document the lives of earlier peoples who passed through the area. It lies in the Sahma desert, which was a stop on the ancient trade route to and from the Arabian Peninsula. This explains the Thamudic inscriptions and writings on the mountain, which date back more than 2,600 years, as well as pre-Islamic Arabic writings and Kufic inscriptions from the first century of the Hijra.

59783298.s: The Mud House Museum is a cultural destination in the city of Tabuk that recreates the life of the forefathers in detail, with its heritage items, and lets visitors learn about the history and heritage of Tabuk at first hand.
59783298.b: The Mud House Museum is a cultural destination in the city of Tabuk. It recreates the life of the forefathers in detail, with its heritage items, and lets visitors learn about the history and heritage of Tabuk at first hand. Visitors are welcomed with Saudi coffee and dates.
59783298.a: 3060 Prince Fahd bin Sultan Road, Al Awayshah

59783132.s: Tabuk Spring, or Ain Sukkar, is a water spring in the city of Tabuk, in the north-west of Saudi Arabia. Its history goes back to the time of the Prophet Muhammad's expedition, and it has continued from then until today.
59783132.b: Tabuk Spring, or Ain Sukkar, is a water spring in the city of Tabuk, in the north-west of Saudi Arabia. Its history goes back to the time of the Prophet Muhammad's expedition, and it has continued from then until today.

59783108.t: Bin Assi Equestrian and Heritage Center
59783108.s: Bin Assi Equestrian and Heritage Center in the Tabuk region brings together horsemanship, purebred Arabian horses and folk heritage. It includes a heritage museum and welcomes tourist delegations and visitors who wish to learn about the heritage of the region.

59783084.t: Waqfa Ala Atabat Al Madi Museum
59783084.s: Waqfa Ala Atabat Al Madi (A Pause at the Threshold of the Past) Museum is one of the most prominent private museums in the city of Tabuk. It has several wings of archaeological and heritage items and welcomes tourist delegations and school students.
59783084.b: Waqfa Ala Atabat Al Madi (A Pause at the Threshold of the Past) Museum is one of the most prominent private museums in the city of Tabuk. It has several wings of archaeological and heritage items and receives visits from tourist delegations, educational institutions and school students.

59783048.s: Al Tawba Mosque, also known as the Archaeological Mosque and called Masjid Al Rasul (the Messenger's Mosque) by the people of Tabuk, dates back to the Expedition of Tabuk in 9 AH, when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) prayed in it for ten nights. The first building of the mosque was in the reign of the Umayyad caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, built of mud, with a roof of palm fronds and carved stones. It was rebuilt in the Ottoman period in 1062 AH (1651 CE), and again in the Saudi era, in the style of the Prophet's Mosque, in 1393 AH.
59783048.b: Al Tawba Mosque, also known as the Archaeological Mosque and called Masjid Al Rasul (the Messenger's Mosque) by the people of Tabuk, dates back to the Expedition of Tabuk in 9 AH, when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) prayed in it for ten nights. 59783042.s: Tabuk Castle is one of the stations on the Syrian Hajj route linking the Levant and the Hejaz. It was built in 967 AH (1559 CE) and restored in the reign of Sultan Mehmed IV, when renovations were added with ceramic tiles that are still at the castle entrance. It was fully restored and renewed again in the reign of Sultan Abdulmejid, son of Mahmud, in 1259 AH (1844 CE), and a special inscription commemorating this was placed in the mosque's mihrab. The castle was renovated again in the Saudi era in 1370 AH (1950 CE), and extensively restored in 1413 AH (1992 CE) by the former Antiquities and Museums Agency of the Ministry of Education.

59783011.s: Tabuk Museum is in Tabuk, in the north of Saudi Arabia, and is housed within the old Hejaz Railway site on a total area of 21,800 square metres, of which the buildings cover about 8,370 square metres. Its main elements include the main hall with the main entrance and reception hall, a VIP hall, prayer rooms for men and women, a gift and souvenir corner and a children's education hall. There are also a presentation hall, a hall on the region's environment, a prehistoric photo hall, a pre-Islamic hall, an Islamic-period hall, a heritage hall, a modern history hall and a lecture hall.

59783006.s: Tabuk Station is one of the stations of the Hejaz Railway and one of its main stops; the first train reached it in 1906. The station is notable for its construction, with a group of buildings laid out in a straight line parallel to the railway track, along with locomotive sheds and maintenance workshops. It has thirteen buildings in a straight line parallel to the track, on an area of about 80,000 square metres. It now lies in the middle of the city of Tabuk and has been restored several times.

59782976.s: Ras Al Sheikh Hamid is a distinctive area for swimming and diving enthusiasts, with clear waters. Visitors can see the mountains of Sharm El Sheikh, Al Tur and the Straits of Tiran, which are no more than 17 kilometres away.

59782973.s: "Tayeb Ism" is a gorge cut through towering mountains, with water flowing through it all year round. At its seaward entrance lies a palm oasis. The gorge is so narrow that only one car can pass at a time. The valley has three springs, the sweetest of which is the one close to the sea.

59782970.s: Magna is a coastal town on the Gulf of Aqaba in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk region, between Haql governorate and Ras Al Sheikh. The village of Magna is about 35 kilometres west of Al Bid' governorate and 235 km from the city of Tabuk. It is known for its beautiful scenery and its two springs, Ain Musa and, 20 km to the north, Ain Tayeb Ism. It is also notable for its many palm, fruit, mango and lemon trees, and for its beautiful seascapes rich in marine life and coral reefs.

59782944.s: Umm Asila Island is one of the islands off the coast of the Tabuk region in the Red Sea. It is a destination for lovers of the sea, quiet nature and boat trips.
59782944.b: Umm Asila Island is one of the islands off the coast of the Tabuk region in the Red Sea. It is a destination for lovers of the sea, quiet nature and boat trips.

59782941.s: Jabal al-Lawz is a mountain in north-western Saudi Arabia, near the Jordanian border in the Tabuk region, about 200 km north-west of the city of Tabuk. It rises 2,549 metres above sea level and is one of the highest mountain ranges in the Hisma region, whose mountains are an extension of the Sarawat Mountains from west of Tabuk to Wadi Rum in Jordan. It is called Jabal al-Lawz (Almond Mountain) because almond trees once grew there. The area has rock art dating back to about 10,000 BC, as well as ancient inscriptions and Islamic writings.
59782941.b: Jabal al-Lawz is a mountain in north-western Saudi Arabia, near the Jordanian border in the Tabuk region, about 200 km north-west of the city of Tabuk. It rises 2,549 metres above sea level and is one of the highest mountain ranges in the Hisma region, whose mountains are an extension of the Sarawat Mountains from west of Tabuk to Wadi Rum in Jordan. It is called Jabal al-Lawz (Almond Mountain) because almond trees once grew there. The area has rock art dating back to about 10,000 BC, as well as ancient inscriptions and Islamic writings. The area flourished commercially because of its distinctive geographic location and took part in the development of civilisation during a particular period, the Nabataean period of the first and second centuries BC and possibly after, which supports evidence of ancient Arab settlement in the area. Snow also falls on the mountain at times in winter, and sometimes in spring when a low-pressure system arrives.
59782941.a: Jabal al-Lawz, Tabuk Province, Saudi Arabia

59782924.s: Mahajjah is a rock formation shaped by erosion and weathering, west of the city of Hail in northern Saudi Arabia and east of the village of Al Jahra. Its walls bear drawings, symbols and some inscriptions carved in different historical periods, some in Aramaic script and others in other languages.
59782924.b: Mahajjah is a rock formation shaped by erosion and weathering, west of the city of Hail in northern Saudi Arabia and east of the village of Al Jahra. Its walls bear drawings, symbols and some inscriptions carved in different historical periods, some in Aramaic script and others in other languages.

59782836.s: Al Naslaa Rock lies in Tayma governorate in the Tabuk region. It is a rock mass about eight metres high, split strikingly into two almost equal halves, and it bears Thamudic inscriptions and ancient rock drawings. Its unique shape has made it one of the best-known natural landmarks in the Kingdom and a destination for photography enthusiasts.

59782830.s: A seaside park on the coast of Haql governorate overlooking the Gulf of Aqaba, visited by locals and visitors for outings, seaside seating and views of the sea and mountains.
